query: France Ebola case 2026: current status of the doctor who tested positive after aid mission, any secondary cases, ECDC reporting. How many confirmed Ebola cases in France as of July 2026?
answer:
I've completed the research. Here's the bottom line on France's 2026 Ebola case:

**Confirmed Ebola cases in France as of July 2026: ONE (1).**

**Key findings:**
- **The case:** A middle-aged male humanitarian doctor (NGO ALIMA) returned from a five-week aid mission in Ituri Province, DRC, arriving at Charles de Gaulle Airport on 23 June 2026. France confirmed the case on 24 June 2026 — the first Ebola case ever confirmed in Europe during the 2026 outbreak and the first to test positive outside Africa.
- **Current status of the doctor:** Recovered and discharged. On 4 July 2026, Health Minister Stéphanie Rist announced full recovery after two negative PCR tests. He was "almost asymptomatic" apart from headaches.
- **Secondary cases:** None. Transmission was imported-only. Five fellow Air France passengers were isolated as a precaution, and WHO listed 107 contacts for follow-up — no onward transmission occurred.
- **ECDC reporting:** WHO declared the Bundibugyo-strain outbreak a PHEIC on 17 May 2026. ECDC rated the EU/EEA general-population risk as "very low," published a threat assessment brief and imported-case preparedness guidance (updated 10 July 2026), and called on Member States to strengthen readiness.
- **Broader context:** WHO DON612 (3 July 2026) counted 1,481 total confirmed cases globally (1,460 DRC, 20 Uganda, 1 France) and 454 deaths; the DRC outbreak later grew to 2,905 cases and 1,269 deaths by 22–23 July 2026.

Full synthesis and structured data (key facts, sources, and quantitative data points) have been delivered via the StructuredOutput tool.
